idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with visible project activity and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • Stop a turn without losing the conversation, and pick up where you left off.
  • Watch what a subagent is doing inside the task that started it.
  • Run your own Claude Code commands, skills and plugins from the panel.
  • See files, commands, tests and relationships in the Activity Map.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Sightline itself writes no transcript; note that the Claude Code CLI keeps its own session history under ~/.claude/projects/, under your account and its own retention rules, which is what lets a conversation resume.

Sightline is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, JetBrains or Google. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "Android Studio" is a trademark of Google. Both are used only to describe compatibility.

Copyright © 2026 Michael Carroll. Source-available — the source is published so it can be read and audited, but it is not open source and may not be redistributed. Using Sightline in your work, including commercially, is expressly permitted. Free during the beta. See the licence accompanying this listing.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.8.0-beta — beta channel. This release changes how Stop, permissions and file writes behave, so it goes to beta first and stable stays on 0.7.0 until it has been driven by hand in a live IDE.

  • Stop now stops the turn, not the session. Pressing Stop interrupts the work in progress and keeps the conversation, the process and its connected MCP servers — your next message just carries on. Press it again to end the process outright. One honest caveat, and Sightline says it rather than hiding it: a command Claude already started keeps running to completion either way, so stopping a build is still yours to do.
  • The permission mode chip actually changes the permission mode. Until now, picking a different mode mid-conversation saved the setting and did nothing else — the chip claimed a policy that was not in force. It now switches the running conversation, and says so; if Claude refuses the switch (Auto needs Sonnet or Opus), you are told in the CLI's own words instead of being left to guess.
  • You can see what subagents are doing. A Task used to render as a wall of raw JSON. It is now a proper card — what was delegated, to which agent, the steps it takes as it takes them, and what it concluded. Skill, SlashCommand, ExitPlanMode, BashOutput and notebook edits are rendered properly too.
  • Claude Code's own commands are in the actions menu. Every command your setup has — built-ins, your project's commands, your plugins' skills — with its description and argument hint, straight from the CLI. Several, like /context and /cost, run locally and cost nothing at all.
  • Fixed: Claude could not see any of the Android tools. Sightline's Android tools were hosted on the MCP server named ide, and the CLI filters that server down to a single tool before the list ever reaches the model — so none of them had ever been callable. They are served under their own name now, and Claude can use them.
  • You are told when the conversation is compacted, and when you hit a rate limit. Both used to pass silently. A compaction replaces earlier messages with a summary, which is why Claude sometimes seems to forget something you told it an hour ago — worth knowing rather than puzzling over.
  • New, off by default: "Revert Claude's file changes to here." Right-click any message you sent and restore the files Claude edited since. It covers edits made with Edit, Write and NotebookEdit — not changes made by a command it ran, and not a subagent's edits inside a Task — and Sightline repeats that every time it asks you to confirm. It rides CLI behaviour that is not part of the documented interface, which is why it ships off and promises nothing.
  • Corrected in PRIVACY.md: Sightline stores no transcript, but the Claude Code CLI it runs keeps its own full session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/. The privacy page said the transcript "never existed on disk", which was true of the plugin and misleading about your machine. It now says where the CLI's copy lives and who clears it.
